data.title: ScienceDaily: A major risk of breast cancer screening may have been overestimated for decades
data.summary: A new analysis suggests mammograms may lead to far less breast cancer overdiagnosis than some earlier studies indicated. Their results were consistent with an overdiagnosis rate below 5%, rather than estimates approaching 30% to 50%.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Zepbound and Mounjaro may turn on the body’s calorie-burning brown fat

data.title: ScienceDaily: REM sleep paradox: Dreaming may drain the brain’s energy even as fuel supply rises
data.summary: Scientists discovered a surprising energy paradox in the brain during REM sleep, the stage most closely associated with dreaming. Blood supply to the brain begins increasing even before REM starts, but neurons’ immediately available energy, measured as ATP, then drops. The finding suggests that dreaming may require such intense internal processing that neurons consume energy faster than it can be replenished.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: REM sleep paradox: Dreaming may drain the brain’s energy even as fuel supply rises

data.title: ScienceDaily: The secret to growing food on Mars could be fungi
data.summary: Scientists think beneficial fungi could help transform nutrient-poor lunar and Martian regolith into a material capable of supporting crops. By helping plants access nutrients and withstand harsh conditions, these microbes could someday make self-sustaining space farming more realistic.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: The secret to growing food on Mars could be fungi

data.title: ScienceDaily: Don’t toss cannabis leaves: They may contain rare compounds with medical potential
data.summary: Scientists discovered rare flavoalkaloids in Cannabis leaves for the first time, along with dozens of other phenolic compounds that had never been reported in the plant. The findings suggest that Cannabis leaves, often discarded as waste, may contain a surprisingly rich source of potentially useful chemicals.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Don’t toss cannabis leaves: They may contain rare compounds with medical potential

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists discovered two bizarre new sea spiders that are “nightmare fuel”
data.summary: Scientists discovered two strange new sea spider species in the Salish Sea, including a hairy-legged, red-eyed species that can groom itself with comb-like appendages. Another is frequently covered in tiny parasites, and researchers say many more undiscovered sea spiders may still be hiding in the region.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists discovered two bizarre new sea spiders that are “nightmare fuel”

data.title: ScienceDaily: This “rare” autism-linked genetic disorder may be far more common than scientists thought
data.summary: A major analysis suggests Phelan-McDermid syndrome, a genetic disorder closely linked to autism, may affect about 1 in 7,300 people and more than 45,000 Americans. Researchers warn that thousands of cases may remain hidden because genetic testing is often not performed, even as targeted treatments move into clinical trials.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: This “rare” autism-linked genetic disorder may be far more common than scientists thought

data.title: ScienceDaily: CRISPR could help doctors attack blood cancer without destroying healthy cells
data.summary: Researchers used CRISPR to remove CD33 from donor stem cells, potentially giving doctors a way to attack aggressive blood cancers without destroying the healthy cells patients need after a transplant. In a 30-patient trial, the edited cells successfully took hold and appeared to shield blood cells from a CD33-targeted cancer treatment.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: CRISPR could help doctors attack blood cancer without destroying healthy cells

data.title: ScienceDaily: CERN has begun disconnecting the Large Hadron Collider
data.summary: CERN has started replacing some of the Large Hadron Collider’s most important magnets as part of its High-Luminosity upgrade. The new superconducting magnets will produce fields about 40% stronger, allowing particle beams to be squeezed more tightly before they collide. That should create far more collisions for the ATLAS and CMS experiments to analyze, giving physicists a much larger window into the fundamental workings of the universe.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: CERN has begun disconnecting the Large Hadron Collider

data.title: ScienceDaily: Quantum computing’s “dark horse” just proved it can go universal
data.summary: Researchers have shown that exotic quantum particles called non-Abelian anyons can perform the full range of operations needed for universal quantum computing. Using 54 qubits on Quantinuum’s H2 processor, they combined braiding and fusion to unlock capabilities that braiding alone could not provide.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Quantum computing’s “dark horse” just proved it can go universal

data.title: ScienceDaily: Earth is tearing apart beneath the Pacific Northwest
data.summary: Scientists have captured a subduction zone off Vancouver Island in the process of tearing itself apart, revealing that these massive tectonic systems may die piece by piece rather than all at once. The discovery could help explain ancient plate fragments, volcanic activity, and how hidden breaks beneath Cascadia may influence future earthquakes.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Earth is tearing apart beneath the Pacific Northwest

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists gave worms magnetic bacteria. They lived 43% longer
data.summary: A magnet-producing bacterium extended the average lifespan of C. elegans worms by more than 43% while helping protect their neurological and intestinal health. Researchers traced much of the effect to suppression of ferroptosis, a damaging form of cell death linked to iron buildup and oxidative stress.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists gave worms magnetic bacteria. They lived 43% longer

data.title: ScienceDaily: “We found something never seen before” – A dead star is producing a shock wave that shouldn’t exist
data.summary: A dead white dwarf with no detectable disk has somehow produced a powerful shock wave that appears to have persisted for at least 1,000 years. Its magnetic field may be partly responsible, but astronomers say an unexplained “mystery engine” may also be at work.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: “We found something never seen before” – A dead star is producing a shock wave that shouldn’t exist

data.title: ScienceDaily: Ancient meteorites reveal a powerful force that helped build the Solar System
data.summary: Ancient grains inside one of the oldest known meteorites reveal that a surprisingly strong magnetic field existed during the solar system’s first 200,000 years. The discovery suggests magnetism worked alongside gravity to help transform a vast cloud of gas and dust into the sun and planetary disk.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Ancient meteorites reveal a powerful force that helped build the Solar System

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists discover an “impossible” cellular survival pathway that could help fight cancer
data.summary: Scientists discovered a surprising backup system that lets mammalian cells make the essential amino acid cysteine even when the pathways once considered indispensable are disabled. The same survival mechanism may help cancer cells resist treatment, raising the possibility that shutting it down could make tumors easier to kill.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists discover an “impossible” cellular survival pathway that could help fight cancer

data.title: ScienceDaily: When what you see doesn’t make sense, your brain does something remarkable
data.summary: The brain may have a built-in way to quickly settle disagreements between regions processing the same scene. Researchers found that matching signals between two visual areas lasted longer, while conflicting signals rapidly faded away. This “consensus building” mechanism could help explain how the brain turns many specialized inputs into one unified view of the world.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: When what you see doesn’t make sense, your brain does something remarkable

data.title: ScienceDaily: Distant time crystals can somehow fall into the same rhythm
data.summary: Researchers have shown that multiple time crystals inside a semiconductor can synchronize their oscillations, much like pendulum clocks gradually falling into the same rhythm. The coupling is carried by spin-polarized electrons, allowing time crystals separated by up to 40 micrometers to lock to a common frequency. The discovery reveals surprisingly long-range connections between these exotic spin systems and could help researchers develop future spin-based devices.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Distant time crystals can somehow fall into the same rhythm

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists thought they knew how this 70-year-old leukemia drug worked
data.summary: A 70-year-old leukemia drug is still revealing new secrets. Researchers found that removing a protein called NUDT5 protected cells from the drug, even though simply blocking the protein had little effect. The unexpected result points to a hidden cellular role that could help explain why people respond differently to certain leukemia treatments.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists thought they knew how this 70-year-old leukemia drug worked

data.title: ScienceDaily: Aging muscles may be losing strength for a reason scientists missed
data.summary: A newly identified breakdown in communication between nerves and muscles could help explain why people lose strength as they age. Researchers were able to improve muscle strength in an animal model by targeting a key protein, raising hopes that some age-related weakness could eventually be treated.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Aging muscles may be losing strength for a reason scientists missed

data.title: ScienceDaily: Scientists find two tiny new snails with shells that close like doors
data.summary: Scientists discovered two tiny new snail species in Montenegro, showing that even Europe still holds animals unknown to science. One lives in the threatened Komarnica Canyon, where a proposed hydropower reservoir could destroy habitat before its full biodiversity is understood.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Scientists find two tiny new snails with shells that close like doors

data.title: ScienceDaily: “We just need to go back” – Uranus’ moon Ariel may have hidden a 100-mile-deep ocean
data.summary: Ariel, one of Uranus’ moons, may once have contained a subsurface ocean more than 100 miles deep beneath its fractured icy shell. The finding, combined with similar evidence from Miranda, suggests the distant Uranian system could harbor multiple hidden ocean worlds.

data.title: ScienceDaily: These massive stars could explain Webb’s strangest galaxies
data.summary: Hubble observations of massive stars in metal-poor dwarf galaxies are revealing clues to why the early universe looks so unusual. Researchers found that stellar winds weaken sharply at extremely low metallicities, potentially allowing massive stars to retain more material and evolve in unexpected ways. The team also found large differences in iron abundance, a key ingredient in stellar winds and supernovae.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: These massive stars could explain Webb’s strangest galaxies

data.title: ScienceDaily: ADHD and autism diagnoses have surged. A massive study may help explain why
data.summary: A large Danish study found that children diagnosed with ADHD or autism today more closely resemble their peers in the general population than those diagnosed 10 years ago. data.title: ScienceDaily: More REM sleep linked to lower risk of 83 diseases
data.summary: A large study tracking more than 95,000 people suggests that how you sleep may be linked to your risk of developing dozens of diseases. People who spent more time in REM sleep had lower risks of 83 conditions, including dementia, heart failure, and Parkinson’s disease, while more deep sleep was associated with lower risks of conditions such as type 2 diabetes and major depression.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: More REM sleep linked to lower risk of 83 diseases

data.title: ScienceDaily: GLP-1 weight loss and diabetes drugs linked to nutritional deficiencies in nearly 1 in 6 children
data.summary: Children taking GLP-1 medications (such as Victoza, Saxenda, Trulicity, and Ozempic) for weight loss, prediabetes, or type 2 diabetes may face an overlooked risk: nutritional deficiencies. https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: GLP-1 weight loss and diabetes drugs linked to nutritional deficiencies in nearly 1 in 6 children

data.title: ScienceDaily: The “big one” might not come alone: Two major West Coast faults may strike back to back
data.summary: The Cascadia subduction zone and northern San Andreas fault may sometimes rupture in rapid succession, according to evidence preserved in 3,100 years of ocean sediments. Researchers identified unusual sediment layers suggesting that earthquakes on the two systems have occurred just minutes to hours apart, including around the massive Cascadia earthquake of 1700. If such synchronization happened again, several major West Coast cities could face emergencies at nearly the same time.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: The “big one” might not come alone: Two major West Coast faults may strike back to back

data.title: ScienceDaily: Breakthrough drug reverses skin aging and dramatically speeds healing
data.summary: A topical drug that removes aging, damaged cells helped older mice heal skin wounds significantly faster. The treatment appeared to reactivate repair pathways involved in inflammation, collagen production, and new blood vessel growth.

data.title: ScienceDaily: Why Viking museums still can’t escape the warrior myth
data.summary: Scandinavian museums are trying to move beyond the familiar image of Vikings as sword-wielding male warriors, highlighting women, farmers, traders, and a far more complicated society. data.title: ScienceDaily: This emerging treatment could help people avoid knee replacement surgery
data.summary: A minimally invasive procedure called genicular artery embolization could offer a new middle ground between conservative treatments and knee replacement for osteoarthritis. Studies suggest the benefits may last two to four years in people who respond well.

data.title: ScienceDaily: Atrial fibrillation patients saw 69% lower risk with common blood thinners
data.summary: Direct oral anticoagulants cut the risk of serious clinical events by 69% in atrial fibrillation patients with an intermediate risk of stroke, according to the randomized SINGLE-AF trial. The benefit was driven mainly by fewer ischemic strokes, with no increase in major bleeding.

data.title: ScienceDaily: One CRISPR treatment cut “bad” cholesterol in half for a full year
data.summary: A single dose of an experimental CRISPR therapy cut LDL cholesterol and triglycerides by about half in patients with difficult-to-treat lipid disorders. The reductions were still present one year later, with the highest dose lowering LDL by 52.5% and triglycerides by 47.8%.

data.title: ScienceDaily: New soil test could reveal how soil microbes help feed plants
data.summary: Scientists have streamlined a method for measuring DNA-bound phosphorus in soil, making it cheaper and easier while preserving its accuracy. https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: New soil test could reveal how soil microbes help feed plants

data.title: ScienceDaily: 1.7-billion-year-old fossils reveal a crucial clue to the rise of complex life
data.summary: Scientists studying ancient Australian rocks uncovered more than 12,000 fossils from some of the oldest known eukaryotes on Earth. These early complex cells lived in settings ranging from coastal mudflats to the open sea, but only where oxygen was available. Oxygen-free environments contained simpler microbes instead. The findings strengthen the idea that oxygen played a crucial role in the emergence of complex life.

https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: 1.7-billion-year-old fossils reveal a crucial clue to the rise of complex life

data.title: ScienceDaily: Why rheumatoid arthritis pain may persist even when inflammation is under control
data.summary: Pain and fatigue in rheumatoid arthritis can persist even after inflammation improves, with depression, poor sleep, obesity, smoking, and chronic pain potentially helping sustain symptoms. https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/20.label: ScienceDaily: Why rheumatoid arthritis pain may persist even when inflammation is under control
